newsitem.title: TAJIKISTAN: Tajik government releases seven rebel fighters.
newsitem.headline: Tajik government releases seven rebel fighters.

text.p: The Tajik government has released seven members of the armed Islamist opposition captured in the former Soviet republic's civil war, officials said on Thursday.
"This was a gesture of goodwill," said Zafar Ikromov, a Tajik government representative on a United Nations-sponsored commission on prisoners.
The men were released on Wednesday evening in a region east of the capital Dushanbe. The news coincided with an announcement of more peace talks.
"The seven former anti-government fighters have already been brought to the Garm region and handed over to local opposition field commanders," Ikromov said in an interview.

Last month, Tajik President Imomali Rakhmonov and opposition leader Sayid Abdullo Nuri agreed to a ceasefire at talks in neighbouring Afghanistan aimed at ending the conflict which has killed tens of thousands of people in the last four years.
The ceasefire appears to be holding and the government has released 13 prisoners since December.

In a further sign of rapprochement, a spokesman for the U.N. military observers in the republic said the Russian government had agreed to host a further round of talks on military and political issues in Moscow, starting on February 26.
"Significant progress has been made in Tehran," the spokesman said of negotiations held earlier this month in the Iranian capital.
However, the opposition complains it has released 111 government servicemen in similar gestures over the same period, and that more than 600 of its fighters are languishing in government prisons.
For its part, the government says 300 of its servicemen are still held hostage in the country's central Tavildara region alone.
And violence continues to stalk the Tajik capital Dushanbe. One of two Russian soldiers wounded in an attack by unidentified gunmen there on Wednesday evening died of his wounds.
"The servicemen were attacked by unknown criminals who used their usual technique -- shooting from a pistol in the back of the head," said Captain Artur Gulko, a Russian military press official.

Gulko said the surviving soldier was in a serious condition. Dozens of Russian servicemen have been killed and wounded in similar attacks in recent months. No one has claimed responsibility for the killings but they have been blamed widely on opposition fighters.
About 20,000 Russian soldiers carry out peacekeeping duties in Tajikistan and guard its remote, mountainous frontier with Afghanistan.
